clue.text: A question of possession

parts.note: the clue describes an interrogative word used to ask who owns something, as in asking about a coat's owner

explanation.definitionFit: This interrogative pronoun asks to whom something belongs, so it literally is a query about ownership.

clue.text: Fight Army volunteers in Greek city

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers going into battle in an ancient Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's reserve of part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Peloponnesian city-state famed for its warriors.

clue.text: What ignorant compilers are?

parts.note: puzzle compilers who write hints would, if lacking knowledge, be both ignorant and without the hints they set

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for knowing nothing, punning on setters who produce clues.

clue.text: Battle to put criminal on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal in prison
a test is a trial or examination

explanation.surface: A fight over whether to bring a crook before the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle or fight for victory, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Continues to make profits

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means goes on or carries on; as a plural noun it means money earned from a sale.

clue.text: Walk over live coals in the heat of battle

parts.note: to cross is to walk over, as over a bridge
glowing coals make a fire

explanation.surface: A firewalker treading hot embers while battle rages around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunfire from two directions at once is a typical hazard at the hottest moment of combat.

clue.text: Betray and defeat industrial workers

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police
to floor an opponent is to knock them down and beat them

explanation.surface: Treachery and a beating aimed at factory staff.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'shop' someone is British slang for informing on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes the factory workforce as opposed to management.

clue.text: City tour arranged around mid-April

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the central letter of the month
the letters of tour are arranged into a new order
the mid-point of the month's name gives its central letter

explanation.surface: A city sightseeing trip organised for the middle of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns TOUR into TRUO; 'around' puts R, the middle letter of April, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city that is the county town of Cornwall in south-west England.

clue.text: Stoic founder adds nothing to Japanese philosophy

parts.note: Zen is the Japanese school of Buddhism
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: The founder of Stoicism contributes nothing to Eastern thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium was the Greek thinker who started the Stoic school.

clue.text: Reunites anew when hungry

indicators.note: making something anew means remaking it, so the letters of reunites are formed again in fresh order

explanation.surface: People coming back together, it seems, when they need food.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for greedy or ravenous.

clue.text: Pretext for offering pardon

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a reason given to justify something; as a verb it means to forgive.

clue.text: But don't spend all your money!

explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means except; as a verb it means keep money back rather than spending it.

clue.text: There's less inclination to leave furtively!

definitions.text: There's less inclination to leave furtively!

parts.words: There's less inclination to leave furtively!
parts.note: a hillside whose gradient decreases is an incline easing off, which also reads as sneaking away

explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning sneak away, punning on a gradient that lessens.

clue.text: Produce simple dress as a stopgap

parts.note: to make is to produce
a shift is a plain straight dress

explanation.surface: Running up a basic frock to tide one over.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary substitute used until something better is available.

clue.text: Sarah has passionate desire for old historian

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
lust is intense desire

explanation.surface: Sarah has a crush on an ancient scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaius Sallustius Crispus was a Roman writer of history.

clue.text: It rarely changes if it's scholarly

indicators.note: the letters of it rarely are changed round into a different word

explanation.surface: A remark that something seldom alters if it is learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to literature or learning, so bookish.

clue.text: Award for artistic society in Lancashire town

indicators.note: the society's letters are placed in the town's name

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, historically in Lancashire
RSA is the Royal Society of Arts

explanation.surface: A prize for an arts group based in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in north-west England; RSA is the Royal Society of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant of money given to a student, so a kind of prize.

clue.text: The Chunnel is in operation

explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Tunnel is a route beneath the sea, a way that runs under; also the word means already started or happening.

clue.text: Energetic socialite returned in torment

indicators.note: returned means the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: live means full of energy, as a live wire
a deb is a debutante, a young society woman

explanation.surface: A lively debutante comes back suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague or harass persistently, so a synonym.

clue.text: No tears when accommodation is gratis

explanation.definitionFit: Read cryptically it is free of rips; as an adjective it describes housing provided without charge.

clue.text: Formal dress needed when monarch receives honour

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Smart clothing required when the king gives out awards.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A long ceremonial gown worn on official occasions.

clue.text: Do the French give state benefit?

parts.note: taken as written
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: Asks whether the French hand out welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for unemployment payments from the government.

clue.text: A gift willingly given

parts.note: willingly puns on a bequest passed on through a will

explanation.definitionFit: A bequest left in a testament, a present made by will.

clue.text: The attack is beginning

explanation.definitionFit: It means an assault on an enemy and also the start of something.

clue.text: Woman embraced by youngster of angelic nature

indicators.note: the woman's word is held inside the youngster's

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A lady hugged by a sweet-natured child.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for one with angelic qualities, a winged child or innocent-looking youngster.

clue.text: Disorder in grange is infuriating

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of in grange are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: A mess in a country house makes someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Making very angry, so a synonym.

clue.text: Previously a warning given by golfers

parts.note: fore is the cry a golfer shouts to warn others of a ball in flight

explanation.definitionFit: An old or dialect word for before.

clue.text: One Pole housed by expert banker

indicators.note: the pieces are housed inside the expert's word

parts.note: a fancier is an enthusiast or connoisseur of something, as a pigeon fancier
I is the Roman numeral one
N stands for North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man lodging with a specialist moneyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manages large sums of money, as a banker does.
